witness.note: Leges Henrici primi: Liebermann’s edited Latin text, from the manuscripts he names in Gesetze I, p. 547, note a, listed below
London, The National Archives (formerly the Public Record Office), E 164/2 (the Red Book of the Exchequer)
The original of the London collection, Leges Anglorum Londoniis collectae (c. 1210), which survives in copies
London, British Library, Cotton MS Claudius A.iii (K1); but for the Quadripartitus and the London texts Liebermann’s K means Cotton MS Claudius D.ii (K2)
John Selden’s manuscript, now lost (known from Twysden’s variants)
Roger Twysden, in Wheloc’s edition of Lambarde’s Archaionomia (Cambridge, 1644)
London, Guildhall (Corporation of London), a lost manuscript (there from at least 1639 to 1721), known only from the variants cited by earlier editors as “Lond”
Manchester, John Rylands Library, MS Latin 155

div.head: Hn 91.4
div.ab: Si murdrum in campis patentibus et passim accessibilibus inueniatur, a toto hundreto communiter, non solum ab eo cuius terra est, suppleatur; si in diuisis accidat, utrimque pertranseat; si in uia regia sit, inde componat cui terra adiacebit.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 607 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: an der Grenze zweier Territorien; vgl. S. 608f inter duas uillas
on the boundary of two territories; cf. p. 608f inter duas uillas
gehe [die Pflicht] auf beide [Territorien] über; vgl. 92, 17
let [the duty] pass to both [territories]; cf. 92, 17

div.ab: If the murdrum is found in open fields, accessible on all sides, let it be made up by the whole hundred jointly, not only by him whose land it is; if it happens on boundaries, let it pass to both sides; if it is on the king's highway, let him to whose land it lies adjacent pay compensation for it.
